posts.author: thalesgal
posts.body:
Hello guys!
So I made my game entirelly 640x480. But I would like to give more options to the player because 640x480 nowadays could be very small on bigger screens. And some players dont want to play fullscreen (alt + enter).
So I would like to ask for a script to add an option to the player to choose the screen size of the game.
I would like a new button option to be added on the MENU and the title screen called "Screen Size"
This button could have like 4 options.
Default (640x480)
1280 x 960
1400 x 1050
Fullscreen (Alt + enter)
*Please note that the game, pictures, and sprites will remain at the default size. It should just stretch just like alt + enter does.
*I have look some scripts through the internet but I just found scripts to resize the entire game. I just want to stretch the screen.
Please let me know if its something possible to do!
Looking forward to some information about that.
Cheers!

posts.author: Artille
posts.body:
This has been quite the journey...
I didn't manage to solve a small bug, which is a black border showing up on title screen, but this is only happening on the title screen
, ingame has no black borders.
I added other resolutions, but you can easily adjust the resolutions you want in the SIZES list
Spoiler:
Screen Resizing Material
Ruby:
# Screen Size Options Script
# Add this script below Materials and above Main

module Screen_Size
  BASE_WIDTH = 544
  BASE_HEIGHT = 416
  COMMAND_NAME = "Screen size"

  SIZES = [
    ["Default", BASE_WIDTH, BASE_HEIGHT],
    ["640x480", 640, 480],
    ["900x600", 900, 600],
    ["1280x960", 1280, 960],
    ["1400x1050", 1400, 1050],
    ["Fullscreen", -1, -1]
  ]

  def self.change_size(index)
    width, height = SIZES[index][1], SIZES[index][2]
    if width == -1 && height == -1
      toggle_fullscreen
    else
      Graphics.resize_screen(width, height)
      resize_window(width, height)
    end
  end

  def self.toggle_fullscreen
    if defined?(Win32API)
      user32 = Win32API.new('user32', 'GetSystemMetrics', 'I', 'I')
      sm_cxscreen = user32.call(0)
      sm_cyscreen = user32.call(1)
      resize_window(sm_cxscreen, sm_cyscreen)
    end
  end

  def self.resize_window(width, height)
    hwnd = Win32API.new('user32', 'GetForegroundWindow', '', 'L').call
    set_window_pos = Win32API.new('user32', 'SetWindowPos', 'LLIIIII', 'I')
    # Get the screen size to center the window
    user32 = Win32API.new('user32', 'GetSystemMetrics', 'I', 'I')
    screen_width = user32.call(0)
    screen_height = user32.call(1)
    x = (screen_width - width) / 2
    y = (screen_height - height) / 2
    set_window_pos.call(hwnd, 0, x, y, width, height, 0x0040)
  end
end

class Window_ScreenSize < Window_Command
  def initialize
    super(0, 0)
    center_window
    select(0)
  end

  def window_width
    return 200
  end

  def make_command_list
    Screen_Size::SIZES.each do |size|
      add_command(size[0], :screen_size)
    end
  end

  def center_window
    self.x = (Graphics.width - window_width) / 2
    self.y = (Graphics.height - window_height) / 2
  end
end

class Scene_ScreenSize < Scene_MenuBase
  def start
    super
    create_command_window
  end

  def create_command_window
    @command_window = Window_ScreenSize.new
    @command_window.set_handler(:screen_size, method(:command_size))
    @command_window.set_handler(:cancel, method(:return_scene))
    @command_window.set_handler(:ok, method(:command_size))
    @command_window.open
  end

  def command_size
    Screen_Size.change_size(@command_window.index)
    return_scene
  end
end

class Scene_Title < Scene_Base
  alias original_create_command_window create_command_window

  def create_command_window
    original_create_command_window
    @command_window.set_handler(:screen_size, method(:command_screen_size))
  end

  def command_screen_size
    SceneManager.call(Scene_ScreenSize)
  end
end

class Window_TitleCommand < Window_Command
  def make_command_list
    add_command(Vocab::new_game, :new_game)
    add_command(Vocab::continue, :continue, continue_enabled)
    add_command(Screen_Size::COMMAND_NAME, :screen_size)
    add_command(Vocab::shutdown, :shutdown)
  end
end

class Window_MenuCommand < Window_Command
  def make_command_list
    add_main_commands
    add_formation_command
    add_save_command
    add_screenSize_command
    add_game_end_command
  end

  def add_screenSize_command
    add_command(Screen_Size::COMMAND_NAME, :screen_size)
  end

  def main_commands_enabled
    $game_system.save_disabled ? false : true
  end
end

class Scene_Menu < Scene_MenuBase
  alias original_create_command_window create_command_window

  def create_command_window
    original_create_command_window
    @command_window.set_handler(:screen_size, method(:command_screen_size))
  end

  def command_screen_size
    SceneManager.call(Scene_ScreenSize)
  end
end
You can rename the option in the Screen_Size module if you want, and you can add, remove or change resolutions to your needs.
I found that some resolutions have some artefacts while others don't, so you probably want to adjust some of them.
I also found that working with multiples of 32 seem to have the best output. But it will work with any resolution nontheless.
EDIT :
To fix the title screen bug, you have to resize your images to 640x480 instead of 544x416, and there will be no more black borders.

posts.author: Zeriab
posts.body:
That's not quite correct. The specific behavior of how the 640x480 in fullmode behaves depends on your drivers and display settings.
I have an Nvidia graphics card. It has the following scaling modes used to determine how lower resolutions are scaled to fit the actual display resolution:
Aspect ratio
Full-screen
No scaling
Integer scaling*
Ref:
https://www.nvidia.com/content/Cont...s/mergedProjects/nvdsp/CS_Display_Scaling.htm
I have added a * to the Integer scaling option because in my experience you cannot rely on it being available. I have had the option being available before, and it works great. But look, I have a GeForce RTX 3080 card yet the option is currently not available for me:
You cannot be sure how the fullscreen mode behaves because it depends on the system settings.
Having the engine do the scaling is a more reliable way if you want to control how the scaling works.
To better explain how integer scaling works in MKXP here are two screenshots I took. (Note: You can freely resize the window in windowed mode)
Windowed mode: (2x)
Fullscreen: (3x)
Note that the linked pictures are what's rendered. These are not 640x480.
MKXP has other scaling options. Here's the default look:
Smoothed and stretched:
